prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2005 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision and priorities
- Argues Britain is heading in the wrong direction under Labour and promises action on five priorities: cleaner hospitals, school discipline, more police, controlled immigration and lower taxes. Pledges equality before the law and governing for all groups.

Economy and tax
- “Value for money” via £12bn annual savings by 2007–08: £8bn to cut borrowing (avoiding future tax rises), £4bn for immediate tax cuts. Freeze civil service recruitment, remove 235,000 posts and cut/abolish 168 public bodies. Overall spending growth limited to 4% a year (vs Labour’s 5%), while matching or exceeding Labour on NHS, schools, transport, international development, police, defence and pensions.
- Pensioner support: halve council tax for many over-65 households (up to £500), restore earnings link for basic state pension, retain Winter Fuel Payments and free TV licences (75+).
- Promote saving: new Lifetime Savings Accounts; strengthen company pensions; use unclaimed assets to protect failed schemes.
- Pro-enterprise: deregulation with departmental “regulatory budgets,” sunset reviews, end “gold-plating” of EU rules; restore opt-out from EU Social Chapter. Keep Bank of England independence; no Euro.

Childcare, schools, skills, universities
- Flexible maternity pay (6 or 9 months). Up to £50/week childcare support per under-5 for working tax credit families, including informal care; support workplace nurseries and clubs for older children.
- Extra £15bn a year for schools by 2009–10; restore discipline by giving heads control of admissions/expulsions and creating Turnaround Schools; cut teacher paperwork and protect against malicious allegations.
- Funding follows the pupil; simplified budgets; exam rigour with published marks; slimmed National Curriculum; option for international qualifications.
- 300,000 vocational grants (£1,000 each) for 14–16s; two hours after-school sport; ban junk food; support school trips.
- Expand parental choice: 600,000 new places; allow state-funded access to lower-cost independent places; moratorium on special school closures; FE reform; scrap university tuition fees and admissions regulator; build university endowments.

NHS and social care
- Raise NHS spending from £1,450 to £2,000 per head; cut bureaucracy (fewer PCTs, abolish SHAs and targets); empower hospitals (matrons, infection control, single rooms); funding follows patients; protect community hospitals.
- Subsidy for self-funded operations (half NHS cost) to cut waits; aim to end waiting lists this Parliament.
- Social care partnership so no one must sell their home; more respite and support for carers; NHS dentistry contracts reform and low monthly payment option.
- Health checks for long-stay immigrants; public STI campaign.

Crime, policing, drugs, terrorism
- 5,000 extra police officers per year; cut paperwork; elected police commissioners; neighbourhood policing with zero tolerance.
- End early release; 20,000 extra prison places; honesty in sentencing.
- Expand rehab to 25,000 residential places; reverse cannabis reclassification to Class B.
- Homeland Security Minister; stronger counter-terror laws and capabilities.

Immigration and borders
- British Border Control Police; 24-hour port surveillance; restore embarkation controls.
- Australian-style points system for work; withdraw from 1951 Geneva Convention and EU asylum control; process claims offshore; annual overall immigration limit, including an asylum quota set by Parliament.

Governance and devolution
- Timetable for Action; ministers accountable. Abolish regional assemblies; return regional powers to local authorities.
- Strengthen Parliament and select committees; cut MPs by 20%; seek largely elected House of Lords.
- English Votes for English Laws; support devolution in Scotland; Welsh referendum on Assembly’s future; uphold consent principle in Northern Ireland.

Communities, housing, transport, environment, rural
- Devolve to councils; stronger planning enforcement incl. on illegal traveller camps; review Human Rights Act impacts.
- Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; expand shared ownership.
- Modernise roads; review speed cameras; longer rail franchises.
- Protect Green Belt; prioritise brownfield; phase out HFCs; incentives for energy-efficient homes; lower VED for low-emission cars; boost recycling; diversify renewables and energy efficiency.
- Support farmers: honest labelling; Little Red Tractor in public procurement; reform CAP; strengthen animal welfare. Free vote to overturn hunting ban.

Defence, foreign policy, Europe, aid
- £2.7bn more than Labour on the Armed Forces frontline by 2007–08; preserve regiments/warships; better procurement; NATO central.
- Iraq: remain to rebuild; pursue Middle East two-state solution.
- Europe: oppose EU Constitution (referendum within six months), no Euro, restore Social Chapter opt-out; seek national control over fisheries; support enlargement incl. Turkey.
- Aid: meet 0.7% of GNI by 2013; increase UK control over aid; champion free trade, rule of law and property rights.

First-month pledges
- Start recruiting extra police, restore matrons, first Budget to cut waste and taxes; empower heads to expel; begin 24-hour port surveillance; set date for EU Constitution referendum and campaign “No.”
